evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Why the system exists

name: Externalise context

name: Intent visible
description: Every requirement traces up to a reason the work exists.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 5 — The model captures *why*, and keeps it inspectable
metadata.measure: The chain from each requirement reaches an intent.
metadata.businessConsequence: Every rule points back to why the work exists.

name: Context survives
description: The reasons survive people leaving and sessions ending.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 5 — The model captures *why*, and keeps it inspectable
metadata.measure: A person judges whether the captured context is actually sufficient. Validation only proves the structure is present.
metadata.businessConsequence: A new person can reconstruct the reasons from the project alone.

name: AI stays outcome-aligned
description: Generated work follows the outcomes rather than a misunderstanding of them.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 5 — The model captures *why*, and keeps it inspectable
metadata.measure: A person judges alignment. The model can show structure, not correctness of intent.
metadata.businessConsequence: A person can tell whether the generated work still serves the outcome.

name: AI understanding inspectable
description: A person can inspect what the AI thought the request meant before anything is built.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 6 — The AI's understanding is inspectable before implementation
metadata.measure: A person judges whether the inferred slice understood the request.
metadata.businessConsequence: You can read what the assistant assumed before any build starts.

name: Reviewers understand at minimum cost
description: A reviewer reaches their next step without a dropped constraint and without wasted effort.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 7 — The reviewer understands the system at minimum cost
metadata.measure: A person judges whether the narrative was short enough and still complete for that role. This is a trade-off, not a pass or fail.
metadata.businessConsequence: The write-up is as short as it can be without hiding a risk the reader owns.

name: Uncertainty visible
description: Unresolved questions stay visible and influence recommendations.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 8 — Unresolved uncertainty is visible, not hidden
metadata.measure: A person judges whether a hidden assumption remains. The register proves the questions that were written down.
metadata.businessConsequence: Open risks stay on a single list, and a recommendation that depends on one says so.

name: Prerequisites verified
description: Significant operations run only after required skills are verified.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 9 — Required skills are verified before significant operations
metadata.measure: The harness halts when a critical skill is missing. A person still judges whether the skill text is the right one.
metadata.businessConsequence: Work stops when a critical skill is missing, and says what to restore.

name: Constraints bound without restricting
description: The constraint language rejects real violations and still accepts a novel solution that conforms.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 10 — The constraint language bounds solutions without restricting them
metadata.measure: A person judges the trade-off between staying in bounds and allowing an unfamiliar conforming solution. OQ-001 asks where the line is.
metadata.businessConsequence: Rules block real violations and still allow a new approach that follows the rules.

name: Verification matches the repo role
description: A repo verifies the scope its role names, against one pinned model, without a second truth.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 11 — A repo verifies against the authoritative model without forking the truth
metadata.measure: A person judges whether role-scoped checks and a single pinned snapshot stay in balance. The requirements are planned.
metadata.businessConsequence: The project checks the right scope and does not keep a second, drifting copy of the truth.

description: A test is a canonical definition in model terms. The authoritative model does not name a runner.

metadata.acceptance: Given the authoritative model, when it is scanned, then no runner product name is required. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

name: Canonical tests are declarative
description: A canonical test states the precondition, the trigger, and the expected result. It does not state selectors or click sequences.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 11 — A repo verifies against the authoritative model without forking the truth
metadata.acceptance: Given a canonical test, when it is read, then precondition, trigger, and expected are present and no selector is required. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

name: Stable semantic locators
description: An element is addressed by a stable test id or an accessible name, not by a stylesheet path or a screen position.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 11 — A repo verifies against the authoritative model without forking the truth
metadata.acceptance: Given a locator, when it is recorded, then it is a test id or an accessible name. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

name: Canonical results
description: A result links to the acceptance it evidenced, the snapshot version, and the run. The model's result is not a runner's private report.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 11 — A repo verifies against the authoritative model without forking the truth
metadata.acceptance: Given a result record, when it is read, then it names the acceptance, the snapshot, and the run. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

name: Deterministic adapter resolution
description: The same canonical test yields the same actions on every run. Inferring a path at run time is forbidden.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 11 — A repo verifies against the authoritative model without forking the truth
metadata.acceptance: Given one canonical test and level-0 recipes, when it runs twice, then the actions match. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

name: Provisioning is separate from execution
description: Setup and teardown are a different adapter, with broader access. The execution adapter has only what a user has. The model names capabilities, not adapter products.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 11 — A repo verifies against the authoritative model without forking the truth
metadata.acceptance: Given the model, when adapters are described, then provisioning and execution are different capabilities. Not enforced in 0.1.0.

name: Secrets are referenced, never embedded
description: No credential appears in the model, the tests, the results, or the repository. The project names the secret. An external store resolves it at run time.

evidence: spec:docs/IOMR-developer-narrative.md#Slice 11 — A repo verifies against the authoritative model without forking the truth
metadata.acceptance: Given the repository, when a future secret scan runs, then only references such as secret names appear. Not enforced in 0.1.0.
metadata.businessConsequence: A credential never appears in the project a person can read. The project names the secret. It does not contain it.
